newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bourse creates market management firm.
newsitem.headline: Italian bourse creates market management firm.

text.p: Italian stock market authorities announced on Friday they had created a new company, Borsa Italiana Spa, to manage the share, over-the-counter and derivatives markets as a step towards privatisation.

Borsa Italiana Spa will have share capital of 200 million lire ($122,000) and interim director will be Benito Boschetto, with three statutory auditors and two acting auditors, a bourse council statement said.
"This is the second important step towards privatisation of the stock markets following the project's approval by (bourse regulator) Consob," the statement said.
The council will remain owner of all the shares in the new company until the Italian Treasury completes placement of the shares on the market.
The council said it would proceed quickly, along with the new company and market members, to working out a code of conduct and rules for managing the market.

On Thursday, the Italian Treasury said it had named KPMG Peat Marwick as financial consultant for the planned privatisation of the stock exchanges, with the advisors given the task of working out a procedure for selling the shares.
The stock market is expected to be privatised later this year.
